title: Jason Calacanis on metrics, B2B lead gen, raising vs bootstrapping, and relentless focus
summary: In this #AskJason call-in, Jason advises founders on which metrics investors care about, how to win enterprise customers bottom-up, and whether to raise venture money. His biggest lesson from 2018: after early traction, narrow focus and scale what works rather than adding new products.

principles.text: Investors want growth plus acquisition channels; solid retention and persona work lets them skip to 'is it growing?'
principles.quote: you're checking off all the boxes and that you're just getting to the meat and potatoes of it which is is this growing or not

principles.text: Assume you can build the product; the question now is whether you can grow it. Be a growth founder.
principles.quote: we assume that you're going to be able to build a great product we assume you're gonna have all the measurement tools let's just get to you know let's just get to the cut to the chase can you grow it

principles.text: Present a numbered list of growth experiments, then triple down on the winners.
principles.quote: here are the 7 experiments we're running this quarter next quarter we're going to run these seven experiments and then we're gonna take the learning from those 14 experiments whichever three do the best we're gonna triple down on them

principles.text: Sell first to the frontline user with a short sales cycle; their feedback and word of mouth beat slow top-down deals.
principles.quote: I prefer you to go after the short sale cycle and the more modest reward not just because it's an easier sale but because of the feedback you're gonna get so you can refine the product

principles.text: Land-and-expand: win users one account at a time on a corporate card and let consensus build upward, as Slack, Yammer and Asana did.
principles.quote: they did not try to go in and win the top-level CTO they said let's win you know this group of developers over here let's win the group of salespeople over here and let them sign up one account at a time

principles.text: Venture money is a fast track: investors demand hypergrowth, and it adds investor management to your workload.
principles.quote: investors do not want slow growth they do not want methodical growth even if they say that they want things to break out they're looking for their uber their Airbnb their Google their Facebook their Instagram
